svg.title: How the system works out a price
svg.text: Each procedure on a booking is priced on its own,
6 base units · 0 modifier units, as published
the procedure inherits from its group
Its own units are blank, so it inherits 6 and 0
Chosen on the booking. Its holder decides who is
billed and whether the price can change. If none
applies: No contract (RVG), offered for every procedure.
Picks the contract version valid on that day
Base, time and modifier units (BTM), plus a note
when modifiers are claimed. A typed price or
discount, with a reason, on adjustable contracts.
Look down the layers. For each field, the first
Blank means inherit; 0 is a value that stops the look.
Units are only starting values: the anaesthetist
can change them on the card.
A fixed price, fixed rate or fixed discount only
ever comes from the contract line for the procedure.
Top to bottom, the first rule that applies sets
the price. Merivale stops at rule 2.
The office's price, with a reason. Works even
or an anaesthetist's own price list.
That price. The recorded BTM is kept for
rate, else the anaesthetist's own unit rate, less
any fixed discount or discount % entered.
The booking is rejected for correction when:
• a price or discount is typed on a locked contract
• BTM is missing and no fixed price applies
• the contract is not valid on the procedure date
The contract decides who gets the invoice.
Patient: the payer on the booking
Name and email, prefilled from the patient and
editable to a parent or guardian.
Snapshot when the List is authorised
Values used, and the layer each came from
Recorded BTM, rate and any discount
Price, and the rule that set it
Later changes to the RVG or a contract never
change an invoice that has been issued.
Five Face-lifts (H3) through the same four steps
Flow: Procedure + contract + date → starting values → price → invoice and snapshot·Still open: multi-procedure rule, prepaid amounts, modifiers
